scenes.location: A local coffee shop near Will's office
scenes.description: Will Parker, a 27-year-old office clerk, meets with his longtime friend, Sarah, and his coworker, Mark, in a quiet corner of the coffee shop. He's visibly tense and has a conflicted look on his face as he explains his decision to take a break from work for the week.

actions.dialogue: Look, I know this is out of the blue, but I'm not going to work this week. I've been thinking a lot lately, and I realize I've been neglecting the important things in my life. I need to take a step back and figure out what's next.
That's a big decision, Will. Are you sure about this? I mean, I know you've been working nonstop, but this feels like a huge shift. What's driving it?
You're not going to work for a whole week? That's not like you, man. I get it, we all need a break, but what about your responsibilities? You've been pushing yourself so hard to get promoted.

I know it's not like me, but I've been feeling like I'm running on a treadmill. I'm working harder than ever, but I'm not actually moving forward. I need to take time to reflect, to grow personally, not just professionally.
I think it's a great idea, Will. Maybe this is the change you've been needing. Let me know if you want to brainstorm what you can do with this time.
Okay, I get it. You've been stressed for a while. Just make sure you don't regret it later, man. But if it helps, I can cover for you at the office if things get too tight.

scenes.plot: Will Parker, typically a workaholic, surprises his friends by deciding to take a week off from his job as an office clerk. He meets with Sarah and Mark at a local coffee shop to explain his decision, which is driven by a growing sense of conflict over his work-life balance and a desire for personal growth. Sarah is supportive and offers to help him plan his time, while Mark is initially skeptical but eventually offers to cover for him at work.
scenes.social_purpose: To illustrate Will's internal conflict and values through a public interaction with friends, showcasing his need for change and how his relationships influence his decisions.
